The prize money on "$8 Million Money Maker" leans toward the smaller prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $8 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

For "$8 Million Money Maker" or any game, being late in a run is not automatically good or bad. The same numbers mean different things near the end of a run.

Every line of $8 Million Money Maker's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
972.headline: How prizes are split

975.body:
The prize money on "$1,000,000 Money Rush" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Today's free summary of "$1,000,000 Money Rush" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
975.headline: Where the prize money is

976.body:
More than the top prize is gone on "100X The Cash". The top two prize levels have no prizes left. With the $2 million and $100,000 prizes all claimed, the biggest prize left is $10,000. The table on this page counts every prize below that.

Everything above about "100X The Cash" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
976.headline: Far less than $2 million to win

980.body:
"20X The Cash" has 276,353 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $10,000 prize, with four left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

The numbers for "20X The Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
980.headline: Prize table details

981.body:
Most of the tickets for "50X The Cash" have been sold. The game is in the last part of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "50X The Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
981.headline: Where this game is in its run

985.body:
MAX-A-MILLION's prizes make it a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of the prize money still unclaimed, most is in wins under $5,000. The prize counts change every day, but this design does not.

If you play "MAX-A-MILLION" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
985.headline: Same price, different prizes

988.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "Emerald 10's" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

If you play "Emerald 10's" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
988.headline: How much has sold

990.body:
"LADY LUCK" has 141,977 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $1,000 prize, with seven left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything above about "LADY LUCK" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
990.headline: A close look at the prizes

992.body:
"$2 MILLION VAULT" has had no $2 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$2 MILLION VAULT" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
992.headline: Top prizes have lasted so far

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has had no $5,000 top prize claimed for five months. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

The numbers for "$5,000 Triple Play" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
993.headline: No top prize claimed lately

994.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "$25,000 Triple Play", about a quarter are still unsold. The game is in the second half of its run, with one of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The numbers for "$25,000 Triple Play" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
994.headline: How much has sold

995.body:
The most common win left on "$200,000 Triple Play" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $5,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "$200,000 Triple Play" comes from official North Carolina lottery numbers, current through November 5.
995.headline: What's actually left to win

996.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$1,000,000 Triple Play" are sold. The top prize count has held, with four of five still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of $1,000,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
996.headline: No top prize claimed lately
